questions.question: A contract requires that prompts and responses are processed only within the EU, while still pooling capacity across EU regions. Which deployment type should you choose?

options.why: Correct. Processing stays within the EU data zone and capacity is pooled across its regions.
Global deployments may process data in any region.
Batch is for offline jobs and processes in any region.
This tier is for testing and does not give a residency guarantee.

questions.explanation: Data Zone deployment types keep processing inside the EU or US zone.

questions.question: A chat app has steady, high daily traffic and needs predictable latency. Which deployment type should you choose?

options.why: Pay-per-token capacity can be throttled at high volume.
This is not a deployment option.
Correct. Reserved PTUs give predictable latency for steady high volume.
Batch returns results within 24 hours and cannot serve interactive chat.

questions.explanation: Provisioned throughput is for steady, high-volume workloads.

questions.scenario: A hospital must keep agent threads, uploaded files and vector data in storage that it owns and encrypts with its own keys.
questions.question: Which Foundry Agent Service setup should you use?

options.why: Correct. It stores threads in your Cosmos DB, files in your Storage account and vectors in your Azure AI Search.
The basic setup stores agent data in Microsoft-managed storage.

options.text: A public deployment with API keys
options.why: Keys relate to authentication and do not control storage ownership.
Batch is a deployment type and does not affect agent storage.

questions.explanation: The standard agent setup uses resources you own.

questions.question: You need two teams to work in one Foundry resource with separate agents, files and access control. What should you create?

options.text: A separate project for each team
options.why: Correct. Projects isolate agents, files, connections and access inside a resource.

options.text: A second deployment for each team
options.why: Deployments pin models and do not isolate agents or files.
DNS zones resolve names and do not separate team workspaces.
Tags organise billing and search but do not isolate access.

questions.explanation: Projects are the workspace boundary inside a Foundry resource.

questions.question: A company must rewrite 50,000 product descriptions by morning at the lowest price. No user waits for the results. Which deployment type should you choose?

options.why: Correct. Batch accepts a file of requests and returns results within 24 hours at a lower price.
This is intended for interactive requests with residency needs.
Reserved capacity costs more than needed for a one-time overnight job.
Interactive pay-per-token capacity costs more and may be throttled.

questions.explanation: Batch is for large offline jobs.
